newsitem.title: THAILAND: Pol Pot almost in tears at trial-Cambodian witness.
newsitem.headline: Pol Pot almost in tears at trial-Cambodian witness.

text.p: Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot was calm during most of his show trial by former comrades but he was almost brought to tears when accused of being as bad as strongman Hun Sen, a Cambodian witness to the trial said on Monday.

The Cambodian who witnessed the July 25 trial in Anlong Veng, northern Cambodia, said most of the people's tribunal that tried Pol Pot was staged, with one person after another denouncing the architect of the Khmer Rouge's 1975-79 "killing fields" reign of terror that killed more than one million Cambodians.
He said Pol Pot was quiet as he listened and appeared to have been briefed on what to expect until one person deviated from the script and compared him to Hun Sen.

"He was so calm and motionless during the trial but when a man shouted from the crowd that Pol Pot was as bad as Hun Sen and deserved to be killed, he was jolted and about to break into tears," the observer, who witnessed the trial and took pictures of Pol Pot, told Reuters.
Second Prime Minister Hun Sen seized power and ousted his co-premier, Prince Norodom Ranariddh, after a July 5-6 power grab in the capital Phnom Penh.

Hun Sen was a mid-ranking Khmer Rouge military commander before breaking with Pol Pot during his 1975-79 rule. Hun Sen later headed a Vietnamese-backed government in Phnom Penh that ruled through the 1980s until an international peace treaty in 1991.
The Khmer Rouge regularly refer to Hun Sen as a puppet of Vietnam. Hun Sen rejects the accusations and has said all Khmer Rouge leaders must face trial for their crimes.
Hun Sen has said the July 5-6 fighting began because he was trying to stop Ranariddh from allowing the Khmer Rouge to infiltrate the capital.
Ranariddh and his FUNCINPEC party had been involved in peace negotiations with the Khmer Rouge before Hun Sen's coup.
The Cambodian observer said despite the condemnation and public trial the crowd of about 500 people appeared to respect Pol Pot and did not use any really strong words when condemning him.
The observer, who led a team to witness the trial, said Pol Pot was not only a mysterious man to the outside world but he was also a stranger for the Khmer Rouge followers who live in Anlong Veng.
"All the people I met and talked with in Anlong Veng said they had never seen Pol Pot until that moment when the old man arrived in a luxury four wheel drive," he said.
He said rebel leaders Khieu Samphan and Ta Mok were not present but their representatives were there to witness the trial.

"Ta Mok told me earlier that he is an old man now and he wanted to retire from all positions in the Khmer Rouge," said the Cambodian observer who played the major role in negotiations with the FUNCINPEC officials.

An article in the Far Eastern Economic Review on the trial last week said Pol Pot was tried and sentenced to life imprisonment because of his efforts to break up his movement following the peace talks.
